caral.name: Caral
caral.summary: An archaeological site in Peru holding the remains of the Caral civilization's main city, about 5,000 years old and considered the oldest city in the Americas.

chinchorro-mummies.name: Chinchorro mummies
chinchorro-mummies.summary: Naturally and artificially preserved remains of the Chinchorro people, the oldest deliberately mummified bodies known, dating from about 5050 BCE; unlike many cultures, they mummified people of all ages and social status, not just elites.

chinchorro-culture.name: Chinchorro culture
chinchorro-culture.summary: A preceramic fishing culture on the coast of what is now northern Chile and southern Peru, lasting from about 7,000 to 1,500 BCE and famous for elaborate mummification; named a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021.

cerro-sech-n.name: Cerro Sechín
cerro-sech-n.summary: An archaeological site in northern Peru dated to 1600 BCE, discovered in 1937, known for stone slabs carved with scenes of human sacrifice among the oldest monumental sculpture in the Andes.

caral-supe-civilization.name: Caral–Supe civilization
caral-supe-civilization.summary: A pre-Columbian society of coastal Peru with as many as thirty major settlements, flourishing from about 3500 to 1800 BCE and recognized as the oldest known civilization in the Americas.

kotosh-religious-tradition.name: Kotosh Religious Tradition
kotosh-religious-tradition.summary: Archaeologists' term for ritual buildings built in the Peruvian Andes highlands from about 3000 to 1800 BCE, found at sites such as Kotosh, Huaricoto and La Galgada; linked to the later Chavín culture.

kotosh.name: Kotosh
kotosh.summary: Archaeological site near Huánuco, Peru, with a sequence of buildings spanning six periods of continuous occupation.

chav-n-de-hu-ntar.name: Chavín de Huántar
chav-n-de-hu-ntar.summary: An archaeological site in Peru with ruins dating back to as early as 1200 BC, serving as a major ceremonial center of the Chavín culture and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

chav-n-culture.name: Chavín culture
chav-n-culture.summary: A pre-Columbian civilization in Peru's northern Andean highlands, flourishing roughly 900 to 250 BCE, marked by an intensified religious cult and advances in ceramics, agriculture, metallurgy and textiles.

julio-c-tello.name: Julio C. Tello
julio-c-tello.summary: Peruvian archaeologist, 1880 to 1947, called the 'father of Peruvian archaeology' for discovering the Paracas culture and investigating Chavín de Huántar.

toribio-mej-a-xesspe.name: Toribio Mejía Xesspe
toribio-mej-a-xesspe.summary: A Peruvian archaeologist and student of Julio César Tello (1896–1983) who discovered the Nazca Lines in 1926 or 1927.

sumer.name: Sumer
sumer.summary: The earliest known civilization, in southern Mesopotamia (now south-central Iraq), emerging between the 5th and 4th millennium BCE; its cities produced the world's earliest known written texts.

paloma-archaeological-site.name: Paloma
paloma-archaeological-site.summary: An archaeological site in Peru dated to roughly 5700 to 2800 BCE, one of the earliest villages in the Americas that archaeologists have been able to date stratigraphically.

quipu.name: Quipu
quipu.summary: Knotted-cord record-keeping devices used by Andean cultures, especially the Inca, to store numbers and other data in a decimal positional system; they date back to at least the 1st millennium CE.

tablachaca-river.name: Tablachaca River
tablachaca-river.summary: A river in Pallasca Province, Peru, whose canyon holds the archaeological site of La Galgada, described as one of the region's most important ceremonial and burial centers.

sechin-bajo.name: Sechin Bajo
sechin-bajo.summary: An archaeological site in Peru with ruins dating from 3500 to 1300 BCE, home to one of the oldest known monumental structures in the Americas.

mara-n-river.name: Marañón River
mara-n-river.summary: The principal source river of the Amazon, rising near Lima, Peru, and flowing through the Andes before joining the Ucayali River.

ruth-shady.name: Ruth Shady
ruth-shady.summary: A Peruvian anthropologist and archaeologist, born 1946, who founded and directs the archaeological project at Caral.

huallaga-quechua.name: Huallaga Quechua
huallaga-quechua.summary: A dialect of the Quechua language spoken in the Central Huánuco region of Peru.

hu-nuco.name: Huánuco
hu-nuco.summary: A city in central Peru, capital of the Huánuco Region, where the Higueras and Huallaga rivers meet.

olmecs.name: Olmecs
olmecs.summary: An early Mesoamerican civilization that flourished roughly 1200 to 400 BC in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco, known for colossal stone heads and considered one of the cradles of civilization.

atacama-desert.name: Atacama Desert
atacama-desert.summary: The driest non-polar desert in the world, a coastal plateau in northern Chile so arid that some stations have never recorded rain and it may have had no significant rainfall for four centuries.
